questions.solution_text: The total number of values the expression 4A+9B will take is 10*15 = 150   To find the number of duplicates, suppose the value is same for two pairs (A2,B2) and (A1,B1)    So, 4A2+9B2 = 4A1+9B1 or, 4(A2-A1) = 9(B1-B2).   This is true only if A2-A1=9 and B1-B2=4   So, A=10 and A1=1. Only one case possible for A's. B1-B2=4 then (B1 can be 5,6,7.............15)  Thus the cases which will repeat are 1. A1=1 B1=5 A2= 10 B2= 1 2. A1=1 B1=6 A2= 10 B2= 2 3. A1=1 B1=7 A2= 10 B2= 3 . .. ... 11. A1=1 B1=15 A2= 10 B2= 11    The number of values B and B1 can take is 11.
